text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ten people die in Monday's skirmishes and riots across the country during rallies calling for minimum constitutional reforms before the general elections to be held later this year.

- The National Convention Assembly (NCA), an opposition-backed alliance, calls on the government to set up a commission to collect public opinion on minimum constitutional reforms and calls on donors to withhold aid to Kenya until the government agrees to reforms.
- The NCA declares a national day of mourning for those who died on the July 7 "Saba Saba" pro-reform rallies.
- At least 31 people are charged in Kisumu, western Kenya with creating disturbances, looting and stoning motorists.
- The Supreme Council of Kenya Muslims (SUPKEM) strongly resents and condemns the use of violence and anarchy in the pursuit of constitutional reforms.
- Security personnel thwart an attempt to break into the late president Jomo Kenyatta's mausoleum by rioters next to parliament buildings during Monday's riots.
- SUPKEM denies having resolved to form a council to place demands for constitutional reforms.
